raw_response:
I’m still doing mostly what has worked for me here in Quzhou, but I won’t put all 10.1 mu into one thing. Wheat and maize are my main steady crops, and I’ll keep that on most of the land because the rotation is familiar and safer for income. But I’ll keep a few mu for chili, because if the market is decent it brings in cash better than grain. I have well water, so I’m not as afraid of dry spells, but pumping costs money, so I won’t water blindly. I finished middle school, so I do listen to the township technician when he talks about fertilizer split and pest timing, but in the end I still go by what I’ve seen on my own fields. Last year wheat and maize responded well when I didn’t cut fertilizer too hard, so this year I’ll stay near my usual rate. Chili takes more labor and more watching, but my family is big even if some work outside, so we can still manage a small area by hand. I’d rather keep grain on most land for stability, then use chili on a smaller piece for extra cash.
